statement: TRACE-MoE has higher 19-class macro-F1 than each baseline
evidence: TRACE-MoE per-class F1 significantly better (Holm p<0.05) than 3/4: bilstm_dnn +9.21 pts (p=0), tfsage_lite +2.28 pts (p=0), transformer +2.61 pts (p=1e-05), rf -2.88 pts (p=0.518)

statement: TRACE-MoE raises the recall of the weakest class (minimum class recall) over the best baseline
evidence: minimum class recall 10.52% vs best baseline rf 20.06% (gain -9.53 pts, needed 5)

statement: On binary detection TRACE-MoE is non-inferior to Random Forest
evidence: binary macro-F1 TRACE-MoE minus RF = +2.419 pts, 95% CI [+2.007, +2.830] over 5 seeds (margin -0.5 pts)

statement: Routing helps: one dense expert of the same size gives lower 19-class macro-F1
The experts specialise by attack family (NMI between expert and category)
Adversarially fine-tuned TRACE-MoE has a lower attack success rate than every baseline
evidence: needs 06_robustness.py with at least one baseline

statement: Adversarial fine-tuning costs little clean 19-class macro-F1
The abstain score detects held-out attack types better than softmax confidence
Abstention lowers the error on accepted traffic more than for any baseline (lowest AURC)
evidence: AURC (lower is better), rank 4/5: rf 0.027, transformer 1.153, bilstm_dnn 1.427, trace_moe 1.711, tfsage_lite 2.026

statement: TRACE-MoE is faster than the Transformer baseline and small enough for an edge gateway
evidence: 685,041 parameters (2.613 MB); 0.0839 ms/window on CPU at batch 1024 vs Transformer 0.0332 ms
